brief: A US equities flow and positioning note. Prime desk: equities net sold a 3rd straight week, driven by single-stock de-grossing, the largest since late July; Industrials sold fastest in 6+ months while Staples/Real Estate were bought, a defensive tilt. Shares desk: ~$20bn net TMT selling over 2 weeks, nearing July's $23bn episode, but unlike July almost no rotation into defensives despite gains in Consumer/Utilities/Financials. Thursday saw a capitulation/de-grossing episode tied to AI financing worries and Iran-Israel-US military escalation risk; the GS Risk Appetite Indicator posted one of its largest drops on record and the NDX-SPX implied vol spread hit a 98th percentile. Desk view: this is a hedge-fund deleveraging episode where short-term stops dominate, so GS says buy the AI-complex dip (Power, Hyperscalers, Inference, Cyber), funded by shorting cyclicals/low-quality. Managed Money kept buying Brent call positions on the geopolitical risk even as put-call skew kept cheapening. Next week: FOMC, hyperscaler and semis earnings, card-network earnings, and the Brazil election (EWZ skew at all-time highs). Single-stock earnings dispersion was wide this week: BMI/EQPT/ALLE/POOL beats versus AVEX/CRS/FPS misses, and MRNA sold off on sell-the-news despite clearing its data bar.
